hero.headline: US and Iran reach tentative ceasefire extension deal
hero.body:
The United States and Iran have reached a tentative agreement to extend their ceasefire, though the arrangement requires final approval from President Trump before taking effect.

Trump announced the extension unilaterally on Tuesday through his Truth Social platform. The decision came after he had earlier suggested military action was imminent, telling CNBC that the US military was "raring to go" and that he did not want to extend the ceasefire, believing the US held a strong negotiating position.

Trump said the extension would continue until Iranian leaders submit a unified proposal for peace. He cited the "fractured" state of Iran's government and stated he was acting upon requests from Pakistan's Prime Minister Shehbaz Sharif and Field Marshal Asim Munir. "I have therefore directed our Military to continue the Blockade and, in all other respects, remain ready and able, and will therefore extend the Ceasefire until such time as their proposal is submitted," Trump wrote.

However, the announcement drew sharp criticism from Iran's negotiating team. Mohammad Bagher Ghalibaf, speaker of the Iranian parliament and the Islamic regime's lead negotiator, rejected the ceasefire extension. His personal adviser, Mahdi Mohammadi, dismissed it as "a ploy to buy time for a surprise strike" and stated that "the losing side cannot dictate terms." Ghalibaf himself said Iran would not accept "negotiations under the shadow of threats" and accused Trump of seeking to turn the negotiating table into a "table of surrender."

The US Navy blockade of Iranian ports remains a major obstacle to restarting negotiations. Iran has demanded the US end the blockade before talks can resume, but Trump and Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent both warned on Tuesday that the blockade will continue. Bessent warned that Iranian oil storage facilities would soon become full, forcing wells to shut down.

A first round of talks in Islamabad ten days earlier ended without agreement on reopening the Strait of Hormuz, the critical waterway Iran closed in the early days of the conflict. That closure has reduced global oil and gas supplies by roughly a fifth and prompted international concern about economic consequences.

Pakistan has continued efforts to mediate between the two sides. Prime Minister Sharif thanked Trump for the ceasefire extension, saying Pakistan would "continue its earnest efforts for a negotiated settlement."

The conflicting statements from Washington and Tehran underscore the deep distrust between the two countries. While some US officials characterize negotiations as progressing, Iranian leadership remains skeptical of American intentions and has suggested preparing for military escalation rather than compromise.

cards.headline: Netanyahu Orders Israeli Military to Seize 70 Percent of Gaza Strip
cards.teaser: Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu directed the army to take control of most of Gaza, violating the current ceasefire agreement.
cards.body:
Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu has directed the military to take control of 70 percent of the Gaza Strip, according to reports from The Guardian and CNN. This order comes amid an active ceasefire agreement between Israel and Hamas.

Netanyahu stated the expanded territorial control would constrain Hamas operations and place the majority of Gaza under Israeli authority. The directive marks a significant escalation of military operations in the region despite the existing ceasefire arrangement.

cards.headline: Israel Strikes Lebanese Capital in Targeted Attack
cards.teaser: Israel conducted a strike in Beirut, escalating tensions as both sides accuse each other of breaking last month's ceasefire.
cards.body:
Israel carried out a targeted strike on Beirut, the Lebanese capital. The city had largely avoided direct attacks until this operation, despite ongoing hostilities in the region.

Both Israel and Hezbollah have accused each other of violating the ceasefire agreement reached last month. The strike on Beirut represents a significant expansion of the conflict into areas that had previously been spared from direct attacks.

cards.headline: Guatemala Agrees to Joint Drug Gang Operations With US
cards.teaser: The agreement allows US forces to conduct joint operations against drug gangs inside Guatemala as part of a broader regional effort.
cards.body:
Guatemala has agreed to conduct joint operations with the United States targeting drug gangs within its borders. The deal expands the Trump administration's campaign to secure agreements for military operations in Latin American countries.

The agreement is part of a broader effort to press Latin American governments to allow joint US operations on their territory. The Trump administration has been pushing multiple countries in the region to agree to similar arrangements for targeting drug trafficking organizations.

cards.headline: Canadian Prime Minister Calls for New Relationship With United States
cards.teaser: Prime Minister Mark Carney said in a New York speech that Canada's distancing from the US benefits both countries.
cards.body:
Canada's Prime Minister Mark Carney delivered a speech in New York calling for a new partnership between Canada and the United States. He used the phrase "help make America great again" in describing his vision for the relationship.

Carney emphasized the need for a "true partnership" that would reimagine economic cooperation between the two countries. He focused on sectors that face challenges from global competition, proposing greater collaboration to strengthen both nations' competitive positions.

cards.headline: Supreme Court sides with death row inmate in racial bias case
cards.teaser: The Supreme Court ruled in favor of a Mississippi man on death row who alleged racial discrimination in jury selection.
cards.body:
The Supreme Court ruled 5-4 in favor of Terry Pitchford, a Black man on death row in Mississippi who was convicted of capital murder. Pitchford challenged his conviction based on claims that Black jurors were systematically excluded from his trial due to racial bias.

The decision allows Pitchford to proceed with his case challenging the jury selection process. He was 18 years old when convicted of murder.

cards.headline: Judge declines to block Trump mail-in voting order
cards.teaser: A federal judge refused to immediately halt Trump's executive order changing mail-in voting procedures.
cards.body:
A federal judge in Washington, D.C. declined to temporarily block President Trump's executive order restricting mail-in voting. The decision allows the administration to proceed with the changes while legal challenges continue.

The judge's refusal to issue an immediate injunction does not constitute a final ruling on the case's merits. Additional judicial rulings on the executive order are expected.

cards.headline: Austrian Man Sentenced to 15 Years for Planning Attack at Taylor Swift Concert
cards.teaser: A court convicted a 21-year-old man who admitted plotting to set off a bomb outside a Vienna concert in 2024.
cards.body:
An Austrian court sentenced a 21-year-old man to 15 years in prison for planning an attack at a Taylor Swift concert in Vienna. The defendant admitted to plotting the attack and other terrorism-related offenses.

Prosecutors said the man planned to detonate a bomb outside the concert venue in 2024. The concert was canceled after authorities learned of the plot. The defendant and another man were also convicted on separate terrorist charges stemming from the investigation.

cards.headline: Portugal Records Hottest May Day as Heatwave Hits Europe
cards.teaser: Portugal broke its record for the hottest day in May as temperatures soared across the continent.
cards.body:
Portugal has broken its record for the hottest day ever recorded in May as extreme heat sweeps across Europe. Italy has issued red alerts in response to the dangerous temperatures affecting the region.

The heatwave is impacting multiple countries. In France, students are sitting exams in schools struggling with intense heat conditions, highlighting the unusual severity of temperatures for this time of year.

cards.headline: Justice Department Opens Criminal Investigation Into Trump Accuser E Jean Carroll
cards.teaser: The department is investigating whether the former columnist lied about funding she received for her civil lawsuit against President Trump.
cards.body:
The US Justice Department has opened a criminal investigation into E Jean Carroll, the former columnist who won a civil lawsuit against President Trump. Investigators are examining whether Carroll made false statements regarding the funding she received for her civil case against the president.

Carroll previously succeeded in her civil suit against Trump, and federal authorities are now scrutinizing the financial backing behind that legal action.

cards.headline: FBI arrests former CIA officer with $40 million in gold bars
cards.teaser: Federal authorities arrested a former senior CIA official after finding millions of dollars worth of gold bars and cash in his Virginia home.
cards.body:
David Rush, a former senior CIA officer, has been arrested and faces charges of theft and making false statements. The FBI discovered approximately $40 million in gold bars and millions in cash at his Virginia home.

Authorities allege Rush removed the gold and cash from a CIA storage space. The materials had disappeared from the agency before investigators located them during their investigation into Rush.

cards.headline: Treasury Department prepares $250 bill with Trump portrait
cards.teaser: Trump appointees at the Treasury Department are pushing for a $250 banknote featuring the president's face.
cards.body:
The Treasury Department is moving forward with plans for a $250 bill featuring Trump's portrait. Trump allies in Congress are working to pass legislation that would make this possible, as federal law currently prohibits printing images of living people on U.S. currency.

Treasury Secretary Bessent has defended the proposal for the commemorative bill. Congressional approval would be required before the new denomination could be printed and distributed.

cards.headline: Michigan Governor Whitmer rules out 2028 presidential run
cards.teaser: Democratic Governor Gretchen Whitmer announced she will not seek the presidency in 2028.
cards.body:
Governor Gretchen Whitmer of Michigan announced she will not run for president in 2028. The decision removes one of the Democratic Party's most prominent figures from the field of potential candidates for the next presidential election.

Whitmer had been mentioned as a possible contender given her national visibility and position as a leading Democrat. Her announcement now clarifies her political plans moving forward.

cards.headline: Man sentenced to 15 years for Taylor Swift concert attack plot
cards.teaser: A 21-year-old Austrian man received a 15-year prison sentence after admitting to planning an attack on a Taylor Swift concert in Vienna.
cards.body:
A 21-year-old Austrian man has been sentenced to 15 years in prison after admitting to planning an attack on a Taylor Swift concert in Vienna. He pleaded guilty to terrorism-related offenses.

Austrian authorities stopped the plot before it could be carried out, preventing a potential attack on the concert venue and its attendees.

hero.headline: Anthropic Raises $65 Billion, Valuation Nears $1 Trillion
hero.body:
Anthropic raised $65 billion in a Series H funding round, reaching a post-money valuation of $965 billion. The artificial intelligence company now stands as the most valuable AI startup, surpassing OpenAI.

The San Francisco-based company develops Claude, an AI assistant that competes directly with OpenAI's ChatGPT. Demand for Claude has surged in recent months, driving the company's rapid valuation increase.

Anthropic's valuation places it among the most valuable private companies globally, approaching the $1 trillion threshold that only a handful of public companies have reached. The funding round represents one of the largest private investment rounds in technology history.

The company plans to use the capital as it prepares for an initial public offering. Anthropic has not announced a timeline for going public, but the substantial valuation and funding suggest the company is positioning itself for a market debut.

Anthropic was founded by former OpenAI executives who left to start a competitor focused on AI safety. The company has attracted significant investment from major technology firms and venture capital funds betting on the continued growth of artificial intelligence applications.

The funding comes as competition intensifies in the AI sector. Multiple companies are racing to develop and deploy large language models and AI assistants for both consumer and enterprise use. Anthropic's ability to raise such a large sum reflects investor confidence in the company's technology and market position.

The $965 billion valuation dwarfs most technology companies and places Anthropic in rare company among private firms. Only a small number of publicly traded companies currently exceed $1 trillion in market capitalization, making Anthropic's valuation particularly notable for a private entity.

Anthropic has not disclosed specific revenue figures or user numbers for Claude. The company competes in a market that includes established players like OpenAI, Google, and Microsoft, all of which have invested heavily in AI development.

cards.headline: S&P 500 and Nasdaq Close at Record Highs
cards.teaser: Major stock indexes reached new closing highs as investors responded to news of an extended ceasefire between the US and Iran.
cards.body:
The S&P 500 and Nasdaq closed at record highs on Thursday, driven by easing geopolitical tensions after the US and Iran extended their ceasefire agreement. Oil prices retreated from earlier gains following the diplomatic development.

Strong corporate profits supported the market's upward momentum throughout the session. Snowflake emerged as a leading performer among individual stocks as investors remained optimistic about economic conditions and earnings growth.

cards.headline: Gap Shares Fall 13% After Retailer Cuts Sales Forecast
cards.teaser: Gap lowered its annual sales outlook following weak performance at Old Navy and Banana Republic.
cards.body:
Gap shares tumbled 13% after the retailer reduced its sales guidance. Old Navy and Banana Republic both underperformed, prompting the company to lower its full-year outlook amid pressured discretionary spending.

The company reported first quarter fiscal 2026 results that missed expectations. Despite the sales forecast cut, Gap raised its full-year earnings per share outlook. The retailer cited challenging conditions for discretionary spending as consumers pull back on non-essential purchases.

cards.headline: Federal Regulator Pauses Review of Union Pacific and Norfolk Southern Merger
cards.teaser: The Surface Transportation Board delayed proceedings on the $85 billion rail merger, requesting additional data.
cards.body:
The Surface Transportation Board conditionally accepted the revised merger application from Union Pacific and Norfolk Southern but paused its review process. The regulator asked for more data before proceeding with the evaluation of the $85 billion deal.

The pause represents a setback for the two railroad giants seeking to combine operations. Union Pacific disputed recent claims from state attorneys general, stating it provided all required answers in its merger paperwork. The merger would create one of the largest railroad networks in North America.

cards.headline: Trump Administration Launches Federal Investment App for Children
cards.teaser: The Trump Accounts app went live, allowing parents to manage $1,000 federal investments provided for each child.
cards.body:
The Trump Accounts app launched Thursday, allowing families to manage federal investment accounts for their children. Each child receives $1,000 in federal funding through the program, with parents able to track and monitor these investments via the application.

Treasury Secretary Bessent announced the app's release earlier in the week. Parents can download the app to access and manage their children's accounts over time.

cards.headline: Oil Prices Ease on Reports of Straits Reopening Agreement
cards.teaser: Oil prices declined from earlier highs as negotiations progressed toward reopening strategic shipping lanes.
cards.body:
Oil prices fell on Thursday following reports of a potential breakthrough in US-Iran talks. The extended ceasefire agreement, pending Donald Trump's approval, prompted the decline in global oil prices.

Earlier in the day, prices had risen after the US reported shooting down four Iranian attack drones, which had raised concerns about the peace deal's viability. The subsequent reports of a possible agreement helped ease those tensions and brought prices back down.

cards.headline: Bari Weiss Names Nick Bilton to Lead 60 Minutes
cards.teaser: CBS editor in chief appointed a tech journalist as executive producer and removed two correspondents.
cards.body:
Bari Weiss, CBS's editor in chief, named Nick Bilton as executive producer of 60 Minutes. Bilton is a tech journalist and filmmaker who will lead the long-running news program.

CBS also fired two on-air correspondents as part of the leadership change. The moves represent a major shake-up for the network's flagship news program. Weiss has been reshaping CBS's news operations since taking the editor in chief role.

hero.headline: Anthropic raises $65 billion at $965 billion valuation ahead of IPO
hero.body:
Anthropic closed a $65 billion Series H funding round at a $965 billion post-money valuation, the artificial intelligence startup announced. The round marks what could be the company's final private fundraise before a planned initial public offering.

The valuation positions Anthropic as one of the most valuable private technology companies. The startup develops large language models and AI systems, competing with companies like OpenAI in the generative AI space.

The size of the funding round reflects continued investor appetite for AI companies despite broader market uncertainty. Anthropic has raised multiple rounds of funding as it develops and scales its AI technology.

The company has not announced a timeline for its IPO. At the current valuation, Anthropic would rank among the largest technology offerings in recent years when it does go public.

Anthropic's valuation growth has accelerated alongside the broader boom in generative AI investment. The company competes in a market where several well-funded players are racing to develop more capable AI systems.

The $965 billion valuation would make Anthropic worth more than most publicly traded technology companies. The figure represents the company's value after the new capital injection.

The funding comes as AI companies face mounting costs to train and operate large language models. These systems require significant computing resources and infrastructure investment.

Anthropic has positioned itself as focusing on AI safety alongside capability development. The company has not disclosed specific plans for how it will deploy the new capital, though scaling operations and research efforts typically require substantial funding in the AI sector.

cards.headline: FBI says Google engineer used internal search data to win $1.2 million on Polymarket
cards.teaser: Federal investigators say a Google employee accessed internal data to place winning bets on prediction markets.
cards.body:
The US Justice Department has charged Michele Spagnuolo, a 36-year-old Google software engineer, with using insider information to place bets on Polymarket. Spagnuolo allegedly leveraged access to data about Google's most-searched terms to make informed wagers on the prediction market platform, earning $1.2 million in profits.

The case marks the second insider trading prosecution linked to Polymarket in recent months. Last month, prosecutors charged a US Army soldier with using classified military information to place bets on the platform regarding potential military action in Venezuela.

cards.headline: Hackers target Signal users with phishing attacks for backup recovery keys
cards.teaser: A new hacking campaign attempts to trick Signal users into revealing the secret keys that unlock their encrypted message backups.
cards.body:
Hackers are conducting phishing attacks to trick Signal users into revealing their secret recovery keys. These keys unlock online backups containing users' past messages, and attackers who obtain them can decrypt and access previously backed-up conversations.

Signal users should be wary of any requests for their recovery credentials, as this new campaign specifically targets these sensitive security credentials to compromise message backups.

cards.headline: Researchers develop new process to extract lithium from rocks
cards.teaser: Scientists created a method to extract lithium from rock sources, potentially diversifying supply of the battery material.
cards.body:
Researchers developed a new process for extracting lithium from rocks, which could help diversify sources of the element used in batteries. The technique offers an alternative to current lithium production methods.

The process targets lithium contained in rock formations. If the method scales up successfully, it could provide additional sources of the material, which is a key component in electric vehicle batteries and energy storage systems.

cards.headline: Apple working to integrate Gemini AI model into iPhone for new Siri
cards.teaser: Apple is attempting to shrink Google's Gemini model to run on iPhone hardware as part of Siri upgrades.
cards.body:
Apple is working to compress and integrate Google's Gemini artificial intelligence model into the iPhone to power an updated version of Siri. The company faces technical challenges in reducing the model's size to fit on mobile devices.

As Apple attempts to shrink Gemini for iPhone use, a cloud-based component will probably be necessary. Large AI models typically require significant computing power, making it difficult to run them entirely on smartphone hardware.

cards.headline: Asana acquires Stack AI, a no-code agent-builder platform
cards.teaser: The project management software company bought Stack AI to expand its artificial intelligence tools.
cards.body:
Asana acquired Stack AI, a platform that allows users to build AI agents without coding. The project management software company plans to integrate Stack AI into its workflow tools.

Asana will incorporate Stack AI into its growing suite of AI-powered features. The acquisition expands Asana's capabilities in artificial intelligence as workplace software companies add more automation features.

cards.headline: Exchanges designing AI token futures as trading instruments
cards.teaser: Major trading platforms are creating derivative products based on AI tokens, treating them like commodities.
cards.body:
Large exchanges are developing derivative products centered on AI tokens, treating them as raw material inputs comparable to electricity or bandwidth rather than purely computational outputs. This shift in perspective mirrors how traditional commodities like gold and oil are traded in financial markets.

These futures contracts would enable traders to speculate on AI token price movements and manage their exposure to the asset class, similar to established commodity futures markets.

hero.headline: Claude Lemieux, four-time Stanley Cup champion, dies at 60
hero.body:
Claude Lemieux, a four-time Stanley Cup champion known for his fierce and physical style of play, has died at age 60. The NHL Alumni Association announced his death on social media, though a cause was not immediately disclosed.

Lemieux built his hockey career on intensity and competitive fire. The winger won Stanley Cup titles with three different teams during his professional career. His contributions to championship teams made him one of the notable figures in modern hockey history.

Among his accomplishments, Lemieux earned the Conn Smythe Trophy in 1995, an award given to the Most Valuable Player of the Stanley Cup playoffs. This recognition reflected his reputation as a performer who elevated his game during the most important moments of the season.

Known for his aggressive approach to the game, Lemieux earned a reputation as a fierce competitor. His style of play sometimes drew controversy, but it also defined his career as a player willing to do whatever was necessary to help his teams succeed.

Following his playing career, Lemieux remained involved in professional hockey. He transitioned into working as a player agent, maintaining his connection to the sport he had helped shape during his years as a competitor.

Lemieux's death marks a significant loss for the hockey community. Players and organizations across the NHL have recognized his impact on the sport and his role in multiple championship runs. His competitive spirit and willingness to play with physicality made him a recognizable figure among hockey fans and within professional circles.

The circumstances surrounding his death and the specific location where he passed away were not immediately clarified in initial reports. The hockey world continues to process the loss of one of its notable champions from recent decades.

Lemieux's legacy extends beyond his individual accomplishments and statistics. His approach to playoff hockey and his ability to perform under pressure influenced how the game was understood during his era. Players and coaches have long pointed to competitors like Lemieux as examples of the mentality required to win championships at the highest levels of professional hockey.

The loss of Lemieux comes as a shock to the broader sports community and to those who followed his career and subsequent work within the sport. His contributions to four Stanley Cup championship teams ensure that his place in hockey history will be remembered as part of the sport's modern era.

cards.headline: Serena Williams in talks for comeback at Queen's Club
cards.teaser: Serena Williams is discussing a potential return to competitive tennis at Queen's Club next month.
cards.body:
The 23-time Grand Slam champion is considering a return to competitive tennis at Queen's Club in London next month. At 44 years old, Williams has been cleared to compete after re-entering the professional drug testing pool six months ago.

Williams is reportedly seeking a doubles wildcard for the event alongside Canadian player Victoria Mboko, ranked 19th in singles. The Queen's WTA 500 tournament begins on June 8, the day after the French Open concludes. Williams last competed professionally in New York in 2022.

cards.headline: Mauricio Pochettino in talks with AC Milan while coaching USA
cards.teaser: USA national team coach Mauricio Pochettino has held initial discussions with AC Milan about becoming their next manager.
cards.body:
Mauricio Pochettino has held initial talks with AC Milan about becoming their next manager, following the Italian club's decision to sack Massimiliano Allegri.

Pochettino currently serves as head coach of the United States men's national team. The discussions with Milan come as the Serie A side searches for new leadership, raising questions about his future with the American program as it opens its World Cup camp.

cards.headline: World number one Jannik Sinner loses in second round at French Open
cards.teaser: Top-ranked Jannik Sinner suffered a shock second-round defeat to Juan Manuel Cerundolo at the French Open.
cards.body:
World number one Jannik Sinner suffered a shock defeat to Juan Manuel Cerúndolo in the second round of the French Open. The Italian star attributed his loss to a lack of energy during the match, rather than the Paris heat affecting his performance.

The upset came as other top players progressed through the tournament. Aryna Sabalenka and Coco Gauff both advanced, while Great Britain's Katie Boulter was eliminated in the second round, losing to 28th seed Anastasia Potapova in three sets.

cards.headline: Connecticut Sun waive Hailey Van Lith for second time this month
cards.teaser: The Connecticut Sun have waived second-year guard Hailey Van Lith after just nine games with the team.
cards.body:
The Connecticut Sun waived Hailey Van Lith, marking the second time the guard has been released in May. Van Lith played only nine games with the team during her brief stint with the franchise.

The Sun activated former first-round draft pick Leila Lacan in a corresponding move. Van Lith was a first-round pick in the 2025 WNBA Draft but has now been cut twice within the same month.

cards.headline: Katie Boulter eliminated as no British players reach French Open third round
cards.teaser: Katie Boulter's loss to Anastasia Potapova means no British players advanced to the French Open singles third round.
cards.body:
Katie Boulter's run at the French Open ended in the second round after losing to 28th seed Anastasia Potapova in a three-set match. The defeat marks the exit of Great Britain's last remaining singles player from the tournament.

With Boulter's elimination, no British players advanced to the third round of the singles competition.

cards.headline: Jaxson Dart addresses Giants teammates after Trump introduction
cards.teaser: Giants quarterback Jaxson Dart spoke to teammates during a team meeting about his introduction of President Trump.
cards.body:
Jaxson Dart addressed his New York Giants teammates during a team meeting to discuss his introduction of President Trump. The quarterback's appearance with the president had sparked discussion within the organization.

Abdul Carter was not present for the meeting, according to reports. The Giants held the gathering as the team worked to address the situation following the Trump introduction controversy.

hero.headline: Austrian Man Sentenced to 15 Years for Plotting Attack on Taylor Swift Vienna Concert
hero.body:
A 21-year-old Austrian man was sentenced to 15 years in prison for planning a jihadist attack on Taylor Swift's concerts in Vienna, which were ultimately canceled in August 2024. The defendant, identified only as Beran A. under Austrian privacy laws, pleaded guilty to terrorism-related charges.

Beran A. admitted to planning an attack targeting concertgoers at Ernst Happel Stadium, where Swift was scheduled to perform three nights. Authorities estimate up to 30,000 people gathered outside the venue nightly, with another 65,000 inside. According to prosecutors, the defendant allegedly intended to use knives or homemade explosives to "kill as many people as possible."

The plot was discovered during a police search of his apartment on August 7, 2024, the day before the concerts were scheduled to begin. Authorities found bomb-making materials at the residence. Investigators determined that Beran A. had studied Islamic State video instructions on constructing shrapnel bombs and had produced a small amount of triacetone triperoxide explosive. He also allegedly attempted to illegally purchase weapons, including a machine gun and hand grenade.

Swift's team canceled all three scheduled performances following the threat. The U.S. provided intelligence that contributed to the decision. In a statement posted to Instagram two weeks later, Swift said the cancellation filled her with "a new sense of fear, and a tremendous amount of guilt because so many people had planned on coming to those shows."

The case extends beyond the Vienna plot. Beran A. and two other men, school friends identified as Arda K. and Hasan E., allegedly planned simultaneous attacks in multiple Middle Eastern cities during Ramadan 2024. While all three traveled to their designated locations, only Hasan E. is believed to have carried out an attack, stabbing a security guard at Mecca's Grand Mosque on March 11, 2024. He remains in custody in Saudi Arabia.

Prosecutors said Beran A. shared Islamic State propaganda through messaging services and networked with other extremist members. According to prosecutors, he swore allegiance to the militant group and discussed acquiring weapons and manufacturing explosives with associates.

Beran A.'s defense attorney, Anna Mair, said her client expressed deep remorse for his actions. "It is also due to the long period of detention that he says it was the biggest mistake of his life," Mair stated outside court.

A Berlin court previously convicted a Syrian teenager of contributing to the Vienna plot, sentencing him to 18 months suspended imprisonment. The attack plot drew comparisons to the 2017 Manchester bombing at an Ariana Grande concert, which killed 22 people.

cards.headline: ABC Submits Station License Renewals Under Protest, Calls FCC Order Unconstitutional
cards.teaser: Disney's ABC filed broadcast license renewals for eight stations while challenging the agency's authority to demand them.
cards.body:
Disney's ABC submitted license renewal applications for its eight local television stations to the FCC as required, but filed them under formal protest. The company contends the FCC's directive is unlawful, arbitrary, and unconstitutional.

The FCC's Media Bureau issued an order last month requiring ABC to reapply for spectrum licenses across all eight of its owned-and-operated stations. ABC met the filing deadline while simultaneously challenging the legal basis for the requirement.

cards.headline: Robyn to Headline San Francisco's Portola Music Festival
cards.teaser: The Swedish pop star will lead the festival lineup alongside Dog Blood and Swedish House Mafia.
cards.body:
Robyn will headline San Francisco's Portola Music Festival in 2026, organizers announced. The Swedish pop artist joins Dog Blood and Swedish House Mafia as top-billed acts for the event.

The festival's full lineup includes Zara Larsson and other artists. Tickets for Portola Festival 2026 will go on sale next week. The festival continues its focus on electronic and dance music with a strong Swedish presence among headliners.

cards.headline: Rambo Prequel Film Set for June 2027 Release
cards.teaser: Lionsgate scheduled the action franchise prequel between major summer tentpoles.
cards.body:
Lionsgate announced a June 4, 2027 release date for John Rambo, a prequel exploring the action franchise's iconic character's earlier years. The film will arrive in a crowded summer window, arriving between Disney's Star Wars: Starfighter and Sony's Spider-Man: Beyond the Spider-Verse.

Warner Bros. is also releasing an Oceans prequel during June 2027, adding to the competitive slate of summer releases.

cards.headline: CNN Announces July 3 Special with Anderson Cooper and Andy Cohen
cards.teaser: The network will air Independence Eve Live, expanding the duo's on-air partnership beyond New Year's Eve.
cards.body:
CNN will air Independence Eve Live with Anderson Cooper and Andy Cohen on July 3, the network announced. The pair will host coverage from an undisclosed location, similar to their New Year's Eve broadcasts from Times Square.

Cooper and Cohen have co-hosted CNN's New Year's Eve coverage for several years. The July special marks their first collaboration outside the year-end time slot. The program will feature fireworks and other Independence Day-related content.

cards.headline: Netflix Releases First Image from Gabriel Martins' On Behalf of My Son
cards.teaser: The streaming service showed Rejane Faria as lead character Vicentina in the Brazilian filmmaker's new feature.
cards.body:
Netflix released the first image from On Behalf of My Son, the new film written and directed by Gabriel Martins. The photo features Rejane Faria in the lead role of Vicentina.

The company unveiled the image at an event in Rio de Janeiro. The Brazilian production is set to premiere in the second half of 2026. Martins previously directed Mars One.

cards.headline: Role Model Announces Third Album Chuck Timely & the Hourglass
cards.teaser: The musician's follow-up to Kansas Anymore will arrive in August.
cards.body:
Role Model announced his third studio album, Chuck Timely & the Hourglass, set for release on August 7. The record follows his previous album Kansas Anymore.

The musician shared news of the upcoming release through his label. No additional details about track listings or collaborators were provided with the announcement.

hero.headline: Court orders Customs chief to testify on tariff refunds process
hero.body:
The U.S. Court of International Trade ordered Customs and Border Protection Commissioner Rodney Scott to appear at a hearing next month to testify about the Trump administration's tariff refunds process.

The court issued the order on Wednesday. The hearing will take place in New York on June 9.

The order comes as questions mount over how the administration is implementing its tariff refunds system. The Court of International Trade handles cases involving international trade and customs laws.

Commissioner Scott will be required to provide testimony about the procedures and policies CBP is using to process refund requests from importers who paid tariffs. The court's decision to compel testimony from the agency's top official suggests judges are seeking direct answers about the program's implementation.

The Trump administration has faced scrutiny over various aspects of its trade policy, including how it handles tariff collections and refunds. The court hearing will provide an opportunity for officials to explain the agency's approach under oath.

CBP, which operates under the Department of Homeland Security, is responsible for collecting tariffs at ports of entry across the country. The agency processes billions of dollars in customs duties annually.

The June hearing will be one of the more high-profile appearances by a CBP commissioner before the trade court. Such orders requiring agency heads to testify personally, rather than sending subordinates, are relatively uncommon and typically indicate the court views the matter as particularly significant.

The tariff refunds process has become a focus of attention as businesses navigate the administration's trade policies. Companies that believe they were charged tariffs incorrectly can file for refunds through CBP, but the process and timeline for such refunds have raised questions among importers and trade lawyers.

cards.headline: Treasury Secretary dodges questions on reported Iran deal
cards.teaser: Scott Bessent told reporters it would be a mistake to get ahead of the president on the reported memorandum of understanding.
cards.body:
Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent declined to address questions about a reported agreement between U.S. and Iranian negotiators during a White House press briefing Thursday, saying it would be premature to discuss the matter before the president. Bessent was filling in for press secretary Karoline Leavitt.

According to U.S. officials, the U.S. and Iran reached a tentative deal to extend a ceasefire. However, Iranian officials have provided conflicting accounts, with some reporting that no deal has been finalized or confirmed.

cards.headline: House Democrats request probe into Trump disaster aid decisions
cards.teaser: Two lawmakers asked the GAO to examine FEMA's criteria for recommending disaster declarations after several high-profile denials.
cards.body:
Representatives Bennie Thompson and Timothy Kennedy have asked the Government Accountability Office to investigate how the Trump administration has handled disaster declarations. The request follows several high-profile rejections of disaster aid requests.

The two Democrats want the GAO to examine the criteria that FEMA uses when recommending whether the president should approve or deny disaster assistance requests.

cards.headline: FEMA chief says agency prepared for hurricane season
cards.teaser: Acting administrator Bob Fenton told CBS News the agency is ready despite the administration's push for states to take more active recovery roles.
cards.body:
Bob Fenton, the acting administrator of the Federal Emergency Management Agency, said the agency is prepared for hurricane season. He made the statement in an exclusive interview with CBS News.

Fenton's assurance comes as the Trump administration pushes for states to take a more active role in disaster recovery efforts. The hurricane season begins June 1 and runs through November 30.

cards.headline: Treasury Department requested designs for $250 bill with Trump's face
cards.teaser: U.S. Treasurer Brandon Beach and his adviser requested prototypes despite federal law barring living people from appearing on currency.
cards.body:
Federal law currently prohibits living people from appearing on U.S. currency. However, Republican lawmakers have proposed creating a $250 bill featuring President Trump to commemorate the nation's 250th anniversary. The proposal would require congressional action to move forward and would need an exception to existing law.

Treasury officials have prepared prototype designs for the commemorative bill, though the legislation authorizing its printing remains stalled in Congress.

cards.headline: Bessent addresses 2028 presidential question at briefing
cards.teaser: The Treasury secretary dismissed a question about his presidential ambitions while filling in for the press secretary.
cards.body:
Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent dismissed a question about his presidential ambitions during a White House press briefing on Thursday. He was filling in for press secretary Karoline Leavitt, who is on maternity leave.

Bessent spoke for more than 30 minutes during the briefing, discussing the Trump administration's negotiations with Iran and the planned launch of Trump Accounts for children.

cards.headline: Bessent criticizes Washington Post reporting on commemorative bill
cards.teaser: The Treasury secretary said he did not understand the article about a planned $250 banknote featuring President Trump.
cards.body:
Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent criticized Washington Post reporting about a planned commemorative $250 bill with President Trump's face on it during the White House press briefing on Thursday.

Bessent asked if anyone from the Post was present and said he did not understand the article. He hosted the briefing while press secretary Karoline Leavitt is on maternity leave.
